target: production atomic Markov trace tr_M(beta_atom; q_0) for p, n, D, T, 3He, 4He via Markov-axiom recursive ascent on the Groebner-Shirshov normal form
target_value: tr_M(beta_atom) computed symbolically in H_{3A}(q) by incremental GS reduction followed by recursive Markov-axiom descent, then evaluated at q_0; emitted at BOTH substrate pins as a deliberate comparison pair
description:
Derivation chain for the production atomic Markov-trace witnesses (PR #516, closing #508) -- the recursive-ascent path that makes A >= 4 feasible where the Hoefsmit path is not. Covers markov-peel-atomic-tr-m.witness.json (proton pin) and markov-peel-atomic-tr-m-muon.witness.json (muon pin) -- 2 witnesses, one per anchor. Trust profile: one AXIOM entrypoint (Hecke energy), one AXIOM (Markov axioms / Finite-Jones uniqueness), two DERIVED steps, one SCRIPT_CITED frontier.

The two witnesses are a SANCTIONED two-pin pair, not a layer straddle: each declares its own q0Anchor, neither mixes pins inside one quantity, and AGENTS.md explicitly allows a comparison producer to carry both.

steps.name: Hecke relation and the balanced q-integer
steps.operation: The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) is the braid-group algebra of B_n modulo (sigma_i - q)(sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0; the eigenvalue separation (q - q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale, the AXIOM entrypoint.

steps.name: Groebner-Shirshov normal form of the atomic braid word
steps.operation: Build the canonical nucleus braid word beta_atom on n = 3A strands and reduce it in H_n(q) by INCREMENTAL Groebner-Shirshov rewriting -- interleaving reduce and multiply so the intermediate term count stays bounded rather than blowing up before the final reduction. The output is the normal-form element, exact in q.
steps.output_value: NF(beta_atom) in H_{3A}(q), a bounded Z[q,q^{-1}]-combination of GS basis elements
steps.notes: Confluence of the GS rewriting system is what makes the normal form well-defined; the Diamond Lemma is the standing citation. Measured bounding: the deuteron's 23-crossing word reduces to 32 terms, 4He's to a form the recursive trace handles end-to-end in ~60 s -- against the Hoefsmit path, which materialises dim-up-to-462 symbolic matrices per partition and is infeasible at A >= 4. The 23 here agrees with the crossing count independently recorded in atomic-braid-recipe-d.derivation.json.

steps.name: Markov-axiom recursive ascent for tr_M
steps.operation: Compute the Markov trace of the normal form by recursive descent on the Markov axioms rather than by summing y_lambda chi^lambda over the Wedderburn blocks: tr_M(x sigma_{n-1} y) reduces via the trace axiom to a trace in H_{n-1}(q) scaled by the Markov parameter z, and the recursion bottoms out at the identity. Uniqueness of the trace satisfying the axioms is the Finite-Jones input, so this and the Wedderburn route compute the SAME functional by construction.
steps.output_value: tr_M(NF(beta_atom)) as an exact rational function of q
steps.notes: The Markov parameter z is the convention-carrying object. Under the canonical convention D, z = q^3/(q^2+1), and the corpus records a structural consequence that needs no source and no anchor to test: the peel's deuteron denominator factors as 192 q^23 (q^2+1)^3 -- ONE (q^2+1) per peel. Convention C (z = sqrt(q)/(q+1)) leaves half-integer powers and cannot produce that factorisation. Recorded from AGENTS.md and computations/markov/peel_anchor_identification_probe.py (PR #5190); NOT independently re-verified in this chain.

steps.name: Evaluation at the substrate anchor -- both pins, deliberately
steps.operation: Evaluate the symbolic trace at q_0 to 30+ digits, once at the experimental (proton) pin and once at the ideal-CAL-2 (muon) pin, emitting a separate witness for each. The pair is the point: their difference IS the mu-p substrate tension propagated through the trace.
steps.notes: The two proton values differ from the two muon values by ~7.9e-8 relative on the proton atom -- the 11.5 ppb anchor tension amplified by the word's q-degree (11 crossings for p). Each witness DECLARES its q0Anchor, so this is the sanctioned comparison pair, not the straddle AGENTS.md forbids: no single computed quantity mixes an ideal-layer input with an experimental-layer one.

steps.name: Cross-check against the Hoefsmit / Wenzl-bridge path
steps.operation: Compare the recursive-ascent trace against the independent Hoefsmit + Wenzl-bridge witness for the atoms both cover, and record the residual per atom.
steps.notes:
script: computations/markov/markov_peel_atomic_witness.py -- the frontier step. Bridge witness: atomic-tr-m-mpfr-50dps.witness.json.

THE RESIDUAL IS NOT ZERO AND THE CHAIN DOES NOT SMOOTH IT. The deuteron differs by 1.86354e-8 -- far above the 50-dps floor either path claims. The witness ATTRIBUTES this to the bridge being colour-blind (it carries `bridge_is_color_blind: true`), i.e. the bridge is the sign-only convention while the peel path is colour-weighted. That attribution is the producer's, and it is NOT independently verified in this chain. Two reasons to keep it flagged rather than accept it: the two conventions differ by a FACTOR OF ~7 on the individual character chi^(6) (1.5599 vs 11.0214, measured in chi-at-q0-sign-only-atomic.derivation.json), so a 5e-8 relative residual on the trace is a much smaller effect than a bare convention swap would suggest; and a ~1e-8 residual on an object claiming 50 dps is exactly the signature that turned out to be STALE WITNESSES rather than a real difference in the chi backends (bean qou-chib). Whether this residual is the colour convention, an anchor difference, or staleness is OPEN.
